analysis: The only change in this PR is one documentation row added to the Runtime constants table in docs/provider/cli-reference.md (head line 2206). It describes the watchdog crash-restart timing: restart at the next check (1-2 min), with defaultGraceSeconds = 300 when the restart would continue a crash-loop chain. It cites WatchdogPolicy.graceSeconds in WatchdogDecision.swift. No source code, config defaults, keys, endpoints or trust boundaries change. I read both base units (1ebf05eb42642970:6 and :7) in full. Neither contains the new row, which is expected because it is head-only. Neither contains any other security-relevant change. The new row relates to T-043 (watchdog rollback authority is the same replaceable binary, TB-003) and to availability. It documents existing behavior and does not alter watchdog trust or crash-loop guard semantics. I did not verify that the 300 s grace value matches WatchdogDecision.swift, because that source is not supplied. A mismatch would be documentation drift, not a security regression. The rest of the document is unchanged context: prefix-cache defaults (T-041), logout and credential handling (A-008), the add-on hold socket (TB-012) and the sandbox installer (TB-013). None of it is modified here, so it is not re-reviewed. Nothing here invalidates a threat-model assumption.
